title: Hikers rescued after search in Jessamine Creek Gorge - NewsBreak
text:
By none ,
1 days ago NICHOLASVILLE, Ky. — Emergency crews from multiple agencies responded April 3 to a report of two lost hikers in the Jessamine Creek Gorge, ultimately locating both individuals and safely escorting them out after several hours of coordinated search efforts.
According to a public disclosure report from the Jessamine County Fire District, crews were dispatched at approximately 5:10 p.m. to the area of Jessamine Gorge Trails. The incident was classified as a public service call involving a citizen assist for lost persons.
Initial reports indicated two hikers were missing, with one suffering from dehydration and exhaustion. Responding agencies included the Jessamine County Fire District, Jessamine County EMS, Jessamine County Emergency Management, Nicholasville Fire Department, Wilmore Fire Department and the Jessamine County Sheriff’s Office.
A staging area was established at Bethel Christian Church on Phillips Lane, while an incident command post was set up at the Jessamine Creek Gorge parking lot. Crews were deployed to multiple access points in an effort to locate the hikers, using mapping technology and coordinated search patterns across the trail system and surrounding creek areas.
Search teams navigated both marked and unofficial trails, eventually locating the hikers near an intersection of Jessamine Creek and an unmarked path. One of the individuals was experiencing difficulty walking and showed signs of physical distress, prompting crews to slow their pace and request additional support.
Emergency personnel on scene provided medical assessment and care before coordinating the hikers’ removal from the gorge. Utility task vehicles were used to transport both individuals and responders back to the staging area.
Both hikers were evaluated further by EMS personnel upon arrival and were later released from care.
In total, four apparatus and nine personnel from the fire district were involved in the response, along with additional support from partner agencies.
The incident remained active for several hours, with crews working into the evening to complete the search, provide care and ensure a safe exit from the rugged terrain.
Officials reminded visitors to remain on marked trails when visiting the Jessamine Gorge Trails and to take necessary precautions, including carrying water and being aware of changing conditions.
